definitions.explanation: Organized activities aimed at promoting, maintaining, or restoring peace, including diplomacy, education, demonstrations, and humanitarian work.

examples.japanese: {国連|こくれん}の{平和活動|へいわかつどう}に{参加|さんか}する。
examples.english: To participate in United Nations peace activities.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}で{平和活動|へいわかつどう}の{一環|いっかん}として{折|お}り{鶴|づる}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: We made paper cranes at school as part of peace activities.

examples.japanese: {広島|ひろしま}と{長崎|ながさき}は{被爆|ひばく}の{経験|けいけん}を{伝|つた}える{平和活動|へいわかつどう}を{長年|ながねん}{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: Hiroshima and Nagasaki have continued peace activities for many years to share the experience of the atomic bombings.

notes:
A compound of {平和|へいわ} (peace) and {活動|かつどう} (activities). Peace activities hold special significance in Japan due to its postwar pacifist constitution and the experiences of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Schools, civic groups, and local governments regularly organize peace-related events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平和活動|へいわかつどう}に{取|と}り{組|く}む: to engage in peace activities
- {平和活動|へいわかつどう}を{推進|すいしん}する: to promote peace efforts
- {平和活動|へいわかつどう}{家|か}: peace activist
- {国際|こくさい}{平和活動|へいわかつどう}: international peace activities

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {平和運動|へいわうんどう}: peace movement — implies a more organized, political campaign
- PKO ({平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}): peacekeeping operations — specifically military or UN-led missions
- {反戦|はんせん}{活動|かつどう}: anti-war activities — focused specifically on opposing war rather than promoting peace broadly
